# Roles and effort

A worker owns a separable result. Planner, researcher, builder, designer, tester
and reviewer describe responsibility, not required extra panes. Preserve the
user's division of priority, dispatch, tracking and integration; one lead can
perform several of these responsibilities.

Select the actual harness, model and supported effort for the judgment required.
Security, consequential concurrency and shared integration need a top-capability
model at high effort unless the owner chooses otherwise. Mechanical work can use
a smaller model when its correctness can be independently checked. More effort
does not repair an unsuitable model. Recheck the pair when an assignment changes.

Read current owner preferences rather than retaining a dated personal model rule.
For Clankie, `clankie fleet status` reports the host size/model targets and notes;
project roles supply hire-profile preferences and worker/role caps. Explicit
owner-authorized hire fields take precedence over preferences.
Inspect the effective project before hiring. These enforced caps are distinct
from host budget targets. An uncertain hire retains its allocation and original
launch choice until reconciled.

Omit model and effort on `hire_agent` to inherit; set them for a resolved
owner-authorized override with a matching harness.
Use the returned effective launch settings as evidence. Changing `clankie model`
or `clankie effort` changes service turns, not an external seat. A pane label or
brief asking for effort is not configuration. Do not change a user's global
harness defaults to tune one worker.

For independent Herdr launches, use the active harness's supported launch flags
from its help and `herdr --skill`. Native children remain within the parent's
session and authority; they do not replace a visible fleet hire when the owner
expects a worker they can watch and address.
